claim.pdf_says: Diagram for Figure D.12 (TEST BEFORE, two conditions). Two return edges are drawn: [Augment identifier-5 with current BY value] loops back LEFT and UP with an arrowhead entering (Condition-2); [Set identifier-5 to current FROM value] loops DOWN, then LEFT along the bottom, then UP with an arrowhead entering (Condition-1).
claim.why_it_matters: In the ASCII rendering the two loop-back edges are dangling: the stubs drawn at Condition-1 and Condition-2 carry '◄' (arrowhead pointing away from the decision) rather than an arrowhead entering it, and the two trailing lines connect the 'Augment identifier-5' and 'Set identifier-5' columns to each other instead of routing back to Condition-2 and Condition-1 respectively. A reader cannot tell which augment/reset step returns control to which test — which is the substance of the PERFORM VARYING figure.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed against the 300 dpi render of PDF page 1186 (printed page 1156) and against E:/Temp/specrecon/v1186/page-1186.md.

PDF, verified by cropping and enlarging the two relevant regions (crop_conds.png, crop_bottom.png):
  * Condition-1 and Condition-2 are each entered from the LEFT by a horizontal line terminating in a solid RIGHT-pointing (filled triangle) arrowhead. Both arrowheads point INTO the decision. Each is fed by a vertical rail rising from the bottom of the chart; Condition-1 is fed by the outer (leftmost) rail, Condition-2 by the inner rail.
  * The 'Augment identifier-5 with current BY value' box (left column, bottom) has a line leaving its LEFT side, running left to the inner rail, then UP into Condition-2.
  * The 'Set identifier-5 to current FROM value' box (right column, bottom) has a line leaving its BOTTOM, running down, then LEFT along the bottom of the chart to the outer rail, then UP into Condition-1.
So the claim's description of the two PDF return edges and their arrowhead direction is accurate.

Markdown (verbatim):
  line 22: '◄──────────╱  Condition-1  ╲── True ──► Exit'
  line 27: '◄─────────╱  Condition-2  ╲── True ──────────────►'
  line 42: '                   |◄──────────────────────────────'
  line 43: '                   └──────────────────────────────►'
The quotes in the claim match the file exactly. Column analysis: the left-column box 'Augment identifier-5' spans cols 8-30 (centre ~19); the right-column rail sits at col 50. Line 42 draws an edge arriving leftward (◄ at col 20) from col 50 into col 19; line 43 draws an edge leaving col 19 rightward to a ► at col 50. The two bottom boxes are therefore wired to EACH OTHER, and neither edge rises to either decision. Meanwhile the '◄' glyphs at column 0 of lines 22 and 27 are left-pointing arrowheads on stubs that terminate at the left margin and connect to nothing — the direction is inverted relative to the printed filled triangles, which point right, into the decision.

This is not reflow, wrapping, hyphenation or page-break furniture: the ASCII rendering encodes a different control-flow graph from the printed one. In a PERFORM VARYING figure the identity of the back edges (which augment/reset step resumes which test) is the entire content of the diagram, so meaning is lost.

One inaccuracy in the claim: it identifies the page as 'Figure D.12 (TEST BEFORE, two conditions)'. The page actually carries Figure D.13, captioned 'The VARYING phrase of a PERFORM statement with the TEST AFTER phrase having one condition' — and the markdown reproduces that caption correctly on line 46. (The printed caption's 'one condition' is itself at odds with the two-decision diagram, but that is an ISO defect, not a transcription defect, and is out of scope here.) The mislabel does not touch the substance of the finding, so real=true with a corrected description below.
verdict.corrected_description: Page 1186 (printed 1156) carries Figure D.13 — 'The VARYING phrase of a PERFORM statement with the TEST AFTER phrase having one condition' (the caption is ISO's; the diagram shows Condition-1 and Condition-2) — not Figure D.12 / TEST BEFORE. In the printed flowchart, both decisions are entered from the left by a line ending in a solid right-pointing arrowhead: 'Augment identifier-5 with current BY value' exits left, runs left to the inner rail and up into Condition-2; 'Set identifier-5 to current FROM value' exits its bottom, runs down, left along the bottom of the chart to the outer rail, and up into Condition-1. The markdown ASCII transcription loses both back edges. The stubs at lines 22 and 27 carry '◄' at column 0 — a left-pointing arrowhead on a segment that dangles at the left margin — the reverse of the printed arrowheads, which point into the decision. The two trailing lines of the block (lines 42-43) instead wire the 'Augment identifier-5' column (col 19) and the 'Set identifier-5' column (col 50) to each other in both directions, so neither back edge reaches a decision. The rendered control-flow graph therefore differs from the printed one, and a reader cannot determine which augment/reset step returns control to which test.
